guarantees.claim: error_o is continuously assigned the internal error signal err.

The FSM state register st is updated by the PRIM_FLOP_SPARSE_FSM macro with next-state input st_gated_d. The st_gated_d signal is a mux: it equals st when block_swcmd is true, otherwise it equals st_d. This causes the FSM to hold its state when block_swcmd is asserted and advance to st_d otherwise. Reset sets st to StIdle.

uncertain_points.claim: The mux-based clock gating condition block_swcmd (line 399) may cause the FSM to hold or advance incorrectly if block_swcmd toggles near the clock edge, creating a glitch hazard. The ICEBOX comment (#14631) indicates this placement is not ideal and prevents explicit clock gating due to the sparse encoding macro.
uncertain_points.cond: block_swcmd changes too close to the clock edge
uncertain_points.risk: Potential corruption of the state machine sequence, leading to incorrect error detection behavior.
